sentences.text: Bullerichthys is an extinct genus containing only one species of arthrodire placoderm, a type of armored fish from the Early Frasnian stage.
This animal belongs to the class Placodermi, a group known for their bony plates covering the head and thorax.
The genus was first described by Dennis and Miles in 1980.
Fossils of this creature have been found in the Gogo Formation in the Kimberley region of Australia.
Researchers believed Bullerichthys was durophagous, feeding on hard-shelled creatures like mollusks.
It is a basal member of the clade Aspinothoracidi, which is part of the major clade Pachyosteomorphi within Eubrachythoraci.
The parent group of the genus Bullerichthys is Aspinothoracidi.
Bullerichthys lived during the Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian period.
Specifically, it lived between 382.31 and 379 million years ago.
